reference-set genre and instrument bias can dominate comparisons

source_updates.limited_conclusion: Disclose reference, N, embedding and preprocessing; report uncertainty or FAD_inf and do not treat FAD as preference or restoration fidelity.

source_updates.limited_conclusion: Useful primary comparator, but parity requires the same full-band target, adaptation policy, reference protocol and raw safety checks.

knowledge_cards: RESTORE mixture consistency excludes HFE and constrains only five existing-band stems.
A separately gainable HFE stem improves auditability but not truthfulness.
Gain-versus-RMS correlation mostly verifies scalar monotonicity rather than semantic disentanglement.
Projection-based music-bleed can miss audible wanted-content damage.
Reference-free FAD still needs a disclosed reference distribution; it means unpaired, not reference-less.
FAD varies with sample count, embedding and reference bias, and VGGish-FAD need not track listening quality.
Thirty synthetic items and point estimates without uncertainty do not establish universal generalization.
RESTORE does not present a parity-controlled full-band HFE comparison with BABE-2.
Cross-hardware runtime and manually timed GUI baselines are not deployment-parity evidence.
SSE degraded-input codec skips require separate preservation and degradation-leakage tests.
Stacked target and residual outputs are not a mixture-consistency guarantee without an explicit sum constraint.
SSE subjective evidence needs complete trial accounting loudness control screening blinding and multiplicity reporting.
